outputs.L1:
An aircraft capable of operating across a range of speeds includes a power plant and an auxiliary turbine. The auxiliary turbine may be a ram air turbine configured to expand and cool an airflow while producing work. The cooled airflow from the auxiliary turbine may be directed to a heat exchange device, such as, but not limited to, a fuel/air heat exchanger.

In one embodiment, the cooled airflow may be used to exchange heat with compressor airflow routed to cool a turbine. Work generated by the auxiliary turbine may be used to power a heating device and to rotate a device that adds work to a shaft of the aircraft power plant. In one form, the aircraft power plant is a gas turbine engine, and the work generated by the auxiliary turbine is used to heat a combustor flow or to drive a shaft coupling a turbine and a compressor.
outputs.L2: An aircraft designed to fly across a range of speeds is equipped with both a main power system and an auxiliary turbine. This auxiliary turbine may take the form of a ram air turbine that extracts energy from an incoming air stream while also expanding and cooling that air. The chilled air leaving the auxiliary turbine may then be supplied to a heat exchanger, including, for example, a fuel-to-air heat exchanger. In one configuration, this cooled air is used to remove heat from compressor air that is being directed toward a turbine for cooling purposes. The energy produced by the auxiliary turbine may also be employed to operate a heating apparatus and to turn a component that contributes mechanical power to a shaft of the aircraft’s power plant. In one version, the power plant is a gas turbine engine, and the output from the auxiliary turbine is used either to heat airflow entering the combustor or to drive a shaft connecting a turbine with a compressor.
outputs.L3:
The aircraft includes a main power plant and an auxiliary turbine configured to operate over a range of rotational speeds and operating conditions. The auxiliary turbine may be integrated into the aircraft system to provide additional functionality beyond conventional propulsion or power generation support.

In one configuration, the auxiliary turbine functions as a ram air turbine. During operation, ram airflow is directed through the auxiliary turbine, where the air expands and cools as it passes through the turbine stages. This expansion process produces useful work while reducing the temperature of the airflow. As a result, the auxiliary turbine can serve both as an energy recovery device and as a source of cooled air for other aircraft systems.

The cooled airflow discharged from the auxiliary turbine may be routed to a heat exchanger. For example, the cooled air may be supplied to a fuel/air heat exchanger, where it can absorb heat from aircraft fuel or another working fluid. This arrangement can improve thermal management by using the temperature drop produced by the auxiliary turbine to support cooling functions elsewhere in the aircraft.

In one embodiment, the cooled airflow from the auxiliary turbine is used to exchange heat with compressor airflow that is directed toward cooling a turbine of the aircraft power plant. Compressor air is often extracted from the power plant and used for turbine cooling; however, this air may be relatively hot. By transferring heat from the compressor airflow to the cooled airflow produced by the auxiliary turbine, the compressor airflow can be reduced in temperature before being delivered to turbine cooling passages. This can improve cooling effectiveness, reduce thermal stress on turbine components, and enhance overall engine efficiency.

The work generated by the auxiliary turbine may also be used in several ways. In one arrangement, the turbine output powers a heating device, such as an electrical resistance heater or another system requiring mechanical or electrical energy. In another arrangement, the auxiliary turbine is mechanically coupled to a shaft of the aircraft power plant so that the work produced by the auxiliary turbine is added to the shaft. This supplemental shaft work can assist the power plant, improve energy utilization, and contribute to more efficient aircraft operation.
outputs.L4:
An aircraft thermal and power management system may be configured to improve the way an aircraft uses incoming air, waste energy, and onboard heat loads. In such a system, an auxiliary ram air turbine is positioned to receive a flow of ram air during aircraft operation. As the ram air passes through the turbine, it expands and drops in temperature. This expansion process produces a cooled airflow that can then be directed to one or more heat exchangers located elsewhere in the aircraft or engine system.

The cooled air produced by the auxiliary ram air turbine may be used to remove heat from a variety of aircraft fluids or engine flows. For example, the cooled airflow can be routed through a heat exchanger to cool aircraft fuel before the fuel is supplied to the engine or used as a heat sink for other systems. In another configuration, the cooled airflow may be used to cool compressor discharge air that is later supplied for turbine cooling. By reducing the temperature of this cooling air, the system can improve the effectiveness of turbine blade, vane, or other hot-section component cooling, which may allow the engine to operate more efficiently or with improved durability.

The auxiliary ram air turbine also recovers useful mechanical work from the expanding airflow. Instead of allowing the pressure and kinetic energy of the ram air to be lost, the turbine converts part of that energy into shaft power. This recovered work may be used in several ways. In one arrangement, it may drive an electrical generator that supplies power to aircraft heating devices, pumps, fans, controllers, or other electrical loads. In another arrangement, the recovered shaft work may be mechanically coupled to a gas turbine engine shaft or an accessory gearbox, thereby supplementing engine power or reducing the amount of power that must otherwise be extracted from the engine.

By combining air expansion cooling with work recovery, the system provides both a thermal management benefit and an energy utilization benefit. The cooled air increases the aircraft’s ability to reject heat from fuel, engine air, or other heat loads, while the turbine work recovery reduces wasted energy and can offset power demands elsewhere in the aircraft. As a result, the aircraft may achieve improved cooling capability, more efficient use of ram air, reduced reliance on conventional bleed-air or electrically powered cooling systems, and improved overall gas turbine engine performance.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract describing an aircraft system with a gas turbine engine, a ram air auxiliary turbine that cools airflow, and uses recovered work for heating or shaft power.
counterfactuals.output: An aircraft system includes a gas turbine engine and a ram air auxiliary turbine arranged to receive an airflow from a ram air inlet. The ram air auxiliary turbine expands the airflow to reduce a temperature of the airflow and provide a cooled air stream for use by one or more aircraft thermal loads, such as an environmental control system, equipment cooling system, or engine cooling circuit. Work extracted from the airflow by the ram air auxiliary turbine is recovered and selectively applied to an aircraft energy demand, including driving a shaft load, assisting rotation of a gas turbine engine spool, driving an electric generator, or powering a heat-producing device. In one configuration, the recovered work is converted to electrical or mechanical power and used to generate heat for anti-icing, cabin conditioning, fuel heating, oil heating, or other aircraft heating functions. A controller may regulate airflow through the ram air auxiliary turbine and distribute recovered work based on aircraft operating conditions, cooling demand, and heating or shaft power demand.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize an invention involving an aircraft power plant and auxiliary turbine where expanded ram air cools compressor air through a heat exchanger and the turbine work assists the engine.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention is an aircraft power-plant arrangement that improves engine efficiency by using ram air both for cooling and for auxiliary power recovery.

In operation, air compressed by the engine compressor is passed through a heat exchanger before entering the combustion system. A separate stream of ram air, taken in from the aircraft’s forward motion, is expanded through an auxiliary turbine. This expansion lowers the ram air temperature, making it an effective cooling medium for the heat exchanger. The cooled compressor air can then be supplied to the engine at a lower temperature, improving thermal efficiency and reducing compressor-discharge heat load.

At the same time, the auxiliary turbine extracts useful work from the expanding ram air. That turbine work is mechanically coupled back to the main power plant, for example to assist the compressor, shaft, or other engine-driven components. Thus, the system both cools the engine’s compressed air and recovers energy from the ram-air stream to help drive the aircraft engine.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a concise technical description of an aircraft capable of operating at multiple speeds using a ram air turbine to provide cooled airflow and mechanical work for a gas turbine engine.
counterfactuals.output: An aircraft includes a gas turbine propulsion system configured for operation across multiple flight speed regimes and a ram air turbine (RAT) exposed to an external airflow during flight. The RAT extracts energy from ram air to drive a mechanical shaft coupled directly or indirectly to one or more components of the gas turbine engine, such as a compressor, accessory gearbox, or generator. Air passing through or around the RAT is expanded and cooled, producing a cooled airflow that is routed to the engine for thermal management, inlet conditioning, intercooling, turbine cooling, or accessory cooling. The system may selectively deploy, bypass, or vary the RAT load based on aircraft speed, engine operating condition, and cooling demand, enabling supplemental mechanical work extraction and improved engine performance over subsonic, transonic, supersonic, or variable-speed operation.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate an abstract for a patent about cooling turbine components with airflow cooled by an auxiliary turbine and using the turbine’s generated work to heat combustor flow or drive an engine shaft.
counterfactuals.output: An engine system includes a main turbine section, a combustor, and a cooling-air circuit configured to deliver cooling air to one or more turbine components. A portion of compressed air is routed through an auxiliary turbine prior to delivery to the turbine components, such that expansion through the auxiliary turbine reduces the temperature of the cooling air. The cooled air is then supplied to blades, vanes, shrouds, disks, or other thermally loaded turbine structures to provide enhanced cooling effectiveness. Work extracted by the auxiliary turbine is utilized within the engine system, including by driving a mechanical load such as an engine shaft or accessory, and/or by supplying heat or work-derived energy to a combustor flow to improve engine efficiency or operability. In some embodiments, the auxiliary turbine is mechanically coupled to a shaft of the engine, while in other embodiments extracted work is converted or transferred to increase the temperature or energy content of air entering or flowing through the combustor. The system thereby reduces cooling-air temperature while recovering useful energy from the cooling-air stream.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in formal patent language, an aircraft propulsion arrangement including an auxiliary ram air turbine, a fuel/air heat exchanger, compressor airflow cooling, and work recovery to the power plant.
counterfactuals.output:
An aircraft propulsion arrangement comprises a power plant including a gas turbine engine having an inlet, a compressor section, a combustor, a turbine section, and an output shaft, and further comprises an auxiliary ram air turbine disposed to be exposed selectively to an external airstream of the aircraft. The auxiliary ram air turbine is mechanically coupled, directly or through a transmission, clutch, variable-speed drive, electrical machine, or hydraulic machine, to the power plant for recovery of work from the external airstream.

In one embodiment, the auxiliary ram air turbine drives an auxiliary compressor arranged to receive ram air and to deliver compressed cooling air to a heat-exchange system. The heat-exchange system includes a fuel/air heat exchanger having a fuel circuit in thermal communication with an air circuit. Fuel supplied to the combustor is routed through the fuel circuit, and at least a portion of airflow compressed by the auxiliary compressor, or bled from the compressor section of the gas turbine engine, is routed through the air circuit, whereby heat is transferred from the airflow to the fuel prior to combustion.

The arrangement further includes a compressor airflow cooling circuit configured to receive airflow from at least one stage of the compressor section and to cool such airflow in the fuel/air heat exchanger before the airflow is returned to the compressor section, supplied to turbine cooling passages, supplied to an environmental-control or accessory system, or otherwise used within the propulsion system. By reducing the temperature of the compressor airflow, the arrangement increases the density of the airflow and reduces compression work, thereby improving overall propulsive efficiency.

The auxiliary ram air turbine is arranged to recover energy from the ram airflow and to return useful work to the power plant. In certain embodiments, the recovered work is supplied mechanically to a shaft of the gas turbine engine. In other embodiments, the auxiliary ram air turbine drives a generator, pump, or compressor, and the resulting electrical, hydraulic, or pneumatic power is supplied to engine accessories, to the compressor airflow cooling circuit, or to a motor-generator coupled to the engine shaft. A control system may regulate deployment, blade pitch, load, clutch engagement, and heat-exchanger flow rates in accordance with flight condition, engine operating condition, fuel temperature, compressor discharge temperature, and power demand.

The fuel/air heat exchanger thereby functions both to cool engine airflow and to heat fuel prior to delivery to the combustor, while the auxiliary ram air turbine provides a source of recovered work that offsets parasitic loads of the cooling system or augments shaft power of the gas turbine engine. The propulsion arrangement thus integrates ram-air energy recovery, fuel heat-sink utilization, compressor airflow cooling, and work return to the power plant in a coordinated aircraft propulsion system.
